title: When a prerequisite may block a learner
statement: What recall evidence a hard prerequisite should demand before it may block a learner is unsettled, since the single-check criterion in use is provisional and uncalibrated.
example: One grade-5 course graph asks for unaided retrieval plus one correct application on a parallel prompt, and gates no learner until that is calibrated.
detail: A grade-5 reading course graph sets the evidence for a hard prerequisite link as unaided point-of-use retrieval plus one correct application on a parallel prompt, with a failure running the named on-ramp and a recheck, and it activates no learner gate before that threshold is calibrated. The course's case for review lists calibrating this provisional criterion as a decision still to make before learner-gated delivery, because the graph can state the retrieval behaviour required but a universal one-check threshold is not empirical learner evidence.

evidence.quote: Calibrate the provisional point-of-use fluency criterion used by hard prerequisite edges.
The graph can state the required retrieval behavior, but a universal one-check threshold is not empirical learner evidence.
Unaided point-of-use retrieval plus one correct application on a parallel prompt; failure runs the named on-ramp and recheck.
No learner gate is active before threshold calibration.
